co_headbanger_s_wall.blurb: Headbanger's Wall is one of the seven walls in Cascade Canyon, a limestone gorge north of Durango, and it holds some of the longer lines in the canyon. Most of the 21 climbs are bolted, with a single trad line and one hard boulder problem mixed in. Expect steep, sustained climbing up arêtes and corners: about half the routes sit in the 5.12 range, the rest split between 5.11 and 5.13, with a lone 5.10. This is not a beginner wall. Several lines face up-canyon and hold shade into the afternoon, which helps on warm summer days. Summer and fall are the usual choice at this elevation, while spring tends to be damp.

co_nebel_horn_ridge.blurb: Nebel Horn Ridge is a conglomerate crag high in Fern Canyon in the southern Flatirons above Boulder, forming the canyon's northern flank. It holds 21 climbs, mostly traditional with a few bolted lines and one aid route, across a wide spread: a handful of easy and moderate routes in the 5.6 to 5.8 range, a solid middle of 5.9 and 5.10, a couple of 5.11s, and a single 5.13 at the top end. Some lines run multiple pitches, and a couple can be top-roped. It is a long hike to reach, which keeps the crowds thin and rewards climbers with some stamina and a taste for wandering.
co_nebel_horn_ridge.approach: Hike the Fern Canyon trail up past the other crags in the canyon, continuing beyond the base of the neighbouring ridge, then cut across to the right and follow a faint path to the rock.

co_wasteland_the.blurb: The Wasteland is a compact limestone cave and wall in Rifle Mountain Park, among the first cliffs developed there and still very popular. All 21 routes are bolted. They are short for Rifle, topping out after roughly 50 to 80 feet, but the climbing is power-oriented and sustained on blue-grey, water-sculpted stone. The grades are hard: nearly all fall in 5.12 and 5.13, with only one route each at 5.10 and 5.11 and a single 5.14. Many older lines have polished holds that make them feel stiffer than their numbers. The walk from the road is just a few steps through brush.

co_acrophile_the.blurb: The Acrophile is a big granite buttress high on the south side of South St. Vrain Canyon, west of Lyons. It is a traditional crag: all 21 routes need a rack, and most follow cracks, including one roof crossed by an offwidth. Routes run roughly 75 to 200 feet. The grades suit solid intermediate leaders, with about a third in the 5.9 range, a good number of 5.10 and 5.11 lines, a few 5.8s and one easy scramble-grade line. The main face catches the sun from midday into late afternoon. Getting to the base takes a stream crossing and a steep, brushy scramble up the slope above the road.

co_fiscal_cliff_the.blurb: The Fiscal Cliff is a small gneiss sport crag on the south side of Clear Creek Canyon, near Golden, a short stroll from the Tunnel 5 area. All 21 routes are bolted, mostly single pitch and about 20 to 80 feet tall. The bulk of the climbing is steep and hard, with over half the routes at 5.12, but there are also a few 5.8 to 5.11 lines for warming up and one easy route. The base sits beside a paved path along the creek, so expect walkers and cyclists passing by, and watch for ticks in season. Direct sun reaches the base of the central routes in mid-afternoon.

_expect.name: Alcove/Pic of the Vic area to the Upper Bridge

co_alcove_pic_of_the_vic_area_to_the_upp.blurb: This stretch of the Uncompahgre Gorge, the Ouray Ice Park, runs from the Alcove past the Pic of the Vic buttress up to the upper bridge, and it carries some of the tallest ice in the park. The 21 routes are mostly single pitch, around 70 to 150 feet, with a few mixed lines. Grades lean hard: about half are WI4, a large share WI5, two reach WI6, and just one is WI3. It is a serious zone, not a place for first-time ice climbers. Most people lower or rappel into the downstream half, and escaping the gorge usually means climbing an ice route out, so plan the day around that.

co_wind_tower_s_face.blurb: The south face of the Wind Tower in Eldorado Canyon is a steep, vertical wall of red sandstone that sees far fewer climbers than the tower's busy southwest side. All 21 routes are traditional, and protection is often sparse, with several routes carrying a runout or serious-fall rating. The approach is brief but steep once across the creek bridge. Grades cluster in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, backed by a handful of 5.9s, a couple of 5.12s and 5.13s, and one easy chimney. Boulderers also traverse and play on the lower part of the wall. This is a good objective for confident, experienced trad leaders.

co_warm_up_traverse_area.blurb: The Warm-up Traverse Area is a sandstone bouldering cluster within the Dark Side, a hillside of problems in Morrison west of Denver. It is probably the densest group of problems on the hill, centred on a long wall with a small cave in the middle and a long traverse, which gives it its name. All 21 problems are boulders, with a friendly bottom end: roughly half sit between V0 and V2, a few V4s fill the middle, and the top end reaches V6 to V8. It works well as a warm-up spot before heading to harder lines elsewhere on the hill. Rattlesnakes are known to live in the area.
